correctness.rationale: A prefix with x_j removals in each group extinguishes exactly the product of the x_j counts. All products vanish before r removals. At t>=r a maximum has no zero coordinates; after assigning one removal per group, maximizing log product amounts to selecting t-r increments from lists log((k+1)/k), k=1,...,a_j-1. Each list decreases strictly, so selecting the largest available increment takes a highest remaining entry and cannot violate precedence. This is precisely the smallest unsaturated count rule, even with ties, and it proves simultaneous optimality at every budget. For a<=b, summing k(k-1), k^2 for k=1,...,a, then a(a+j) for j=1,...,b-a, gives a(a^2+3b^2+3b-1)/6. Under a<b the initial degrees force the smaller side first, giving ab(b+1)/2; the difference a(a^2-1)/6 is positive exactly when a>=2. The frozen subset recurrence chooses the final vertex, with minimum initial degree when restricted, and is exact. An independent direct edge-score permutation census checked all 1,099 labeled simple graphs of orders 1–5 and all orders, found no strong degree failures through four, and found exactly the ten labeled K_{2,3} graphs at five, each scoring 13 versus 12. Order zero, if allowed, is immediate.
residual_risks: The all-size claim requires complete Cartesian-product incidence; the census is exact only through five and assumes a simple graph without repeated passive partner pairs. The strict bipartite degree comparison is only for 2<=a<b.

The other nearby ecological record optimizes degree allocations under random primary losses, not an ordering on a fixed incidence graph.

value.rationale: Initial-degree ranking is a natural baseline in the established application. The result both supplies a single optimal ranking for every removal budget in a transparent family and identifies the smallest structure that makes all degree tie-breakings fail. The useful content of the small computation is the complete sharp obstruction and its interpretation, not the one-unit score difference alone.
residual_risks: No implication for typical empirical networks, dynamic responses to loss, weighted graphs or general-purpose ranking algorithms is claimed.
